prompt.context_jp: 今回、放射線科の面々が向き合うの___、生きた患者ではなく、物言わぬ遺体の写真である。
prompt.prompt_jp: 今回、放射線科の面々が向き合うの___、生きた患者ではなく、物言わぬ遺体の写真である。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that frames the nominalized clause as the topic being contrasted with 'not living patients, but photos of corpses.'

feedback.correct_en: は marks 'what they face this time' as the topic being characterized, setting up the Xではなく Y contrast that follows.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce it as new information or exhaustive listing, which doesn't fit the explanatory 'as for X, it is Y' structure of the narration.

contrast_examples.jp: 向き合うのは遺体の写真である。
contrast_examples.en: What they face is photographs of corpses. (topic)

prompt.context_jp: この奇跡のようなツールをもってしても 絶対に 繋がれない相手___いる
prompt.prompt_jp: 絶対に 繋がれない相手___いる
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle introducing the existence of 'someone we cannot connect with' as new information.

feedback.correct_en: が introduces the existence of this unseen 'other party' as new information to the listener — a classic 〜がいる existential pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose that the 'party' is already a known topic, but the narration is revealing it for the first time.

contrast_examples.en: There is such a person. (new info)
As for that person, he exists. (known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 扉が開き、白衣姿の杏が顔をのぞかせる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 五十嵐の背筋___、目に見えて跳ねた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that reports Igarashi's spine suddenly reacting — a fresh, observed event.

feedback.correct_en: が presents the sudden observable reaction as new information — the narrator is reporting what happens in that instant.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat 'his spine' as an established topic being described, losing the sense of a sudden visible event.

contrast_examples.en: His back is sturdy. (description of topic)

prompt.context_jp: いや ですが 院長
prompt.prompt_jp: 私たち 医者の仕事___ 患者を救うことです
prompt.prompt_en: Kaburaki defines what their job is. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: は marks 'our job as doctors' as the topic being defined — classic X は Y です definition.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would imply 'OUR job (as opposed to others')' is to save patients, an exhaustive reading that contradicts the general-statement tone here.

contrast_examples.jp: 仕事は患者を救うことです。
contrast_examples.en: Our job is to save patients. (definition)
The work is hard. (describing a situation)

prompt.context_jp: うちの病院じゃ Ａｉのスペシャリストなの 威能___
prompt.prompt_jp: うちの病院じゃ Ａｉのスペシャリストなの 威能___
prompt.prompt_en: The sentence puts the predicate first and names 威能 at the end as the topic. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: は marks 威能 as the topic in this right-dislocated structure — 'the Ai specialist, that's Ino (as a topic).'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn it into exhaustive identification ('it is Ino who…'), which doesn't fit this casual tag-on introduction.

contrast_examples.jp: スペシャリストなの、威能は。
威能がスペシャリストだ。

prompt.context_jp: 到着時には 既にＣＰＡで 蘇生対象ではありませんでした
prompt.prompt_jp: 心臓付近に擦過傷___見られ 他に目立った外傷がないので
prompt.prompt_en: The doctor reports a newly observed finding on the body. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: が introduces the abrasion as a newly observed finding — this is clinical reporting of what was seen.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose the abrasion as a known topic, which doesn't fit a fresh observation being communicated for the first time.

contrast_examples.en: The abrasion is small. (known topic described)

prompt.context_jp: 死んだ人間を写真に撮って
prompt.prompt_jp: 死んだ人間を写真に撮って 何の意味___ あるんですか？
prompt.prompt_en: The father throws back a rhetorical question. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: が is standard in the question 何がある(んですか) — asking what thing (new info) exists as 'meaning' in such an act.
feedback.incorrect_en: は with 何 is ungrammatical as a plain question subject — 何は〜 does not work the way 何が〜 does here.

prompt.context_jp: 杏が遺族を説得する場面
prompt.prompt_jp: Ａｉ___ あなたたち遺族のために やるべきなんです
prompt.prompt_en: An makes a thesis statement about what Ai is for. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: は treats Ai as the topic and makes a general claim about it — 'As for Ai, it should be done for you.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively identify Ai as 'the one thing' to do, which conflicts with the thematic, persuasive tone of the sentence.

contrast_examples.en: Ai is the thing that should be done. (identification)

prompt.context_jp: お兄ちゃんが死んじゃったのは
prompt.prompt_jp: 僕___せいだ
prompt.prompt_en: Yuta blames himself — 'it is MY fault.' Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: の is the genitive linking 僕 to せい ('my fault'). This is the correct possessive attachment.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would ungrammatically split 僕 from せい; 僕はせいだ does not mean 'it's my fault.'

contrast_examples.en: I'm the one who did it.

prompt.context_jp: どうしても 重ねちゃうんだろ
prompt.prompt_jp: 自分___ 父親だから 一応
prompt.prompt_en: Igarashi explains why the chief is affected. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: も ('also') fits: 'he himself is ALSO a father (like the victim's dad), so he projects onto them.'
feedback.incorrect_en: は would just mark 自分 as topic without conveying the inclusive 'also like them' meaning that drives the empathy.

contrast_examples.en: Because he too is a father.
He himself is a father. (plain assertion)

prompt.context_jp: 現制度の解剖で 最も深刻な問題になってんの___ 児童虐待だ
prompt.prompt_jp: 現制度の解剖で 最も深刻な問題になってんの___ 児童虐待だ
prompt.prompt_en: Onodera identifies the single most serious problem. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: は in the 〜のは〜だ cleft frames 'what has become the biggest problem' as topic and points to child abuse as the answer.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would put the emphasis on 'the one that has become a problem,' but after なってんの the cleft naturally takes は.

prompt.context_jp: 受話器を置いた小野寺
prompt.prompt_jp: 母親___ Ａｉを承諾した
prompt.prompt_en: Onodera reports breaking news to the team. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: が delivers this as fresh news — 'the mother (specifically, not the father) has consented' — carrying both newness and exhaustive focus.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame the mother as a known topic being described, flattening the breaking-news impact of the announcement.

contrast_examples.en: As for the mother, she consented. (contrast — implies father didn't)

prompt.context_jp: なぜ線量を多く設定するのか
prompt.prompt_jp: 線量が多ければ多いほど 画像___ 高画質になります
prompt.prompt_en: Igarashi explains the general principle. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: は marks 画像 as topic in a generic statement — 'as for images, they become higher quality.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce 画像 as new info, but the sentence is a general causal rule, not reporting a new finding.

prompt.context_jp: 藤本さんは 左手に時計をしているので
prompt.prompt_jp: 藤本さん___ 左手に時計をしているので 右利きですよね？
prompt.prompt_en: Igarashi addresses Fujimoto and makes a claim about him. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: は treats 藤本さん as the topic being described (he wears his watch on the left, so he's right-handed).
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it exhaustive identification, which doesn't match a direct-address description like this.

contrast_examples.jp: 藤本さんは右利きです。
藤本さんが右利きです。
contrast_examples.en: It's Mr. Fujimoto who is right-handed. (exhaustive)

prompt.context_jp: 直樹君の所持品を見た時
prompt.prompt_jp: あるはずの携帯電話___ ありませんでした
prompt.prompt_en: Igarashi reports what he noticed was missing. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: が in the negative existential 〜がない introduces the missing phone as a newly observed fact — a key clue he's revealing.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose the phone as an established topic. The point here is the discovery of its absence, which calls for が.

prompt.context_jp: 杏はテーブルに用意した皿を父の席___揃え
prompt.prompt_jp: 用意した皿を父の席___揃え
prompt.prompt_en: She arranges the dishes toward her father's seat. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: に marks the goal/destination where the dishes are placed and arranged (父の席に揃える).
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark the location where an activity happens, but 揃える here means arranging items TO a spot, which needs に.

contrast_examples.en: Line the dishes up at the seat. (goal)

prompt.context_jp: 杏が肺の濃淡の写真を見せる
prompt.prompt_jp: 呼吸による___ですね
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the technical term Igarashi uses for the blurring caused by breathing on an image.

feedback.correct_en: アーチファクト (artifact) is the standard radiology term for a non-pathological image distortion caused by motion like breathing.
feedback.incorrect_en: エコー refers to ultrasound; ノイズ is generic noise. Neither captures the specific 'motion artifact' meaning used in imaging.

contrast_examples.jp: 動きによるアーチファクトです。

contrast_examples.en: The image has a lot of noise.

prompt.context_jp: 致命的な外傷がないからって
prompt.prompt_jp: 心臓振とうとは___ないだろ
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the expression meaning 'not necessarily' / 'doesn't mean.'

feedback.correct_en: 〜とは限らない ('not necessarily') is the fixed expression. 限んない is the casual contraction of 限らない.
feedback.incorrect_en: ならない and 違わない do not form the set 'not necessarily X' pattern needed here.

contrast_examples.jp: 心臓振とうとは限らない。
contrast_examples.en: It's not necessarily a cardiac concussion.

prompt.context_jp: 父を残していく後ろめたさは
prompt.prompt_jp: ___にしもあらずだった
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the archaic set phrase meaning 'not nonexistent / somewhat present.'

feedback.correct_en: なきにしもあらず is a literary idiom meaning 'it is not that it doesn't exist' — i.e. there was indeed some guilt.
feedback.incorrect_en: ありにしもあらず and ないにしもあらず are not real forms; the idiom fixes なき (classical negative attributive).

contrast_examples.jp: 疑いはなきにしもあらず。
contrast_examples.en: There is a certain suspicion (not nonexistent).

prompt.context_jp: Ａｉの実施の件ですが
prompt.prompt_jp: もう一度 考え___ いただけないでしょうか
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the polite request verb meaning 'reconsider.'

feedback.correct_en: 考え直していただけないでしょうか is the polite 'could you reconsider' structure — て-form of 直す plus いただく.
feedback.incorrect_en: 直った is intransitive past (doesn't fit with いただく); bare 直し lacks the needed て-form to connect to いただけない.

contrast_examples.jp: 考え直していただけますか。

prompt.context_jp: 結構 詰まってんだけど
prompt.prompt_jp: Ａｉなら ___ないね
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the expression meaning 'can't be helped / have to accept it.'

feedback.correct_en: しかたない ('it can't be helped') shows reluctant acceptance — she's full but will make room because it's for Ai.
feedback.incorrect_en: いけない means 'must not,' and つかない doesn't form the needed idiom. Neither conveys resigned acceptance.

contrast_examples.jp: 忙しいけどしかたない。
contrast_examples.en: I'm busy, but it can't be helped.

prompt.context_jp: そんな思いをずっと
prompt.prompt_jp: そんな思いをずっと___ながら 生きてくのは 苦しいことだと思います
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the verb that collocates with 思い meaning 'bearing / carrying.'

feedback.correct_en: 思いを抱える is the standard collocation for 'carrying (painful) feelings' — fitting the emotional weight An describes.
feedback.incorrect_en: 持つ is too plain/generic; つける doesn't collocate with 思い this way. 抱える specifically evokes burden.

prompt.context_jp: もう 何をしても 何の意味もない
prompt.prompt_jp: そう___ました
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the verb matching 'I thought (that way).'

feedback.correct_en: そう思っていました ('I had been thinking that way') uses 思う with ていました for an ongoing past belief.
feedback.incorrect_en: 考えました/感じました would also need the ていました form; bare 考え and 感じ don't connect correctly here, and 思う is the natural verb for 'that's what I thought.'

contrast_examples.en: I had been considering it so. (more analytical)

prompt.context_jp: 検視に来る警察には
prompt.prompt_jp: 警察には ___なければなりません
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the verb for 'must speak to (the police).'

feedback.correct_en: 警察に話す ('talk to the police') is the natural collocation for giving a statement — more conversational than 言う.
feedback.incorrect_en: 言う is too direct/declarative, and 伝える suggests one-way message delivery. 話す best fits speaking with investigators.

contrast_examples.jp: 警察に話さなければならない。
contrast_examples.en: We have to talk to the police.

prompt.context_jp: 杏が明日の不確かさについて呟く
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for An's wistful line?

choices.text: 誰だって 明日も 今日と同じように 生きてるかなんて 分からないんですよね
誰も 明日も 今日と同じ 生きるか なんて 分かりますよね
誰だって 明日も 今日と一緒 生きてるかどうか 知らないよね

feedback.correct_en: The original phrasing flows naturally: 誰だって… 生きてるかなんて 分からない captures the reflective, slightly colloquial tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: B inverts polarity (分かりますよね contradicts the meaning) and uses stilted syntax. C mixes 誰だって with 知らない in a way that feels off for a professional's quiet remark.

contrast_examples.jp: 誰だって明日は分からない。
誰も明日が分かりますよね。

prompt.context_jp: 五十嵐が雄太に優しく話しかける
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural as Igarashi's gentle reassurance to a child?

choices.text: 他にさ 原因があるかもしれないから もう少しだけ 待っててね
他に 原因 ある かもしれない から もう少し 待つ ね
原因が他にあるかもしれないので、もう少々お待ちください

feedback.correct_en: A uses the soft discourse marker さ and 待っててね, which naturally fits a casual, gentle talk to a child.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is choppy and dictionary-form; it doesn't sound like natural speech. C is overly formal business language unsuited to speaking with a frightened kid.

contrast_examples.jp: もう少しだけ待っててね。
contrast_examples.en: Just wait a little longer, okay? (to a child)

contrast_examples.jp: もう少々お待ちください。

prompt.context_jp: 威能が褒められて答える
prompt.prompt_en: Which response sounds most natural for a modest brush-off of praise?

choices.text: いや それほどでも
いえ、とても大きいです
いや、そんなに多くないです

feedback.correct_en: それほどでも(ない) is the set humble response to being praised — 'not really that much.'
feedback.incorrect_en: B praises himself (opposite meaning). C talks about quantity, not modesty — it doesn't function as a modest brush-off.

contrast_examples.jp: ありがとうございます。

prompt.context_jp: 杏が母親に尋ねる
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for asking why someone changed their mind?

choices.text: あの… どうして 心変わりを？
あの… なんで 心が変わりますか？
あの… 心変わりはどうでしたか？

feedback.correct_en: どうして心変わりを(されたのですか) is a natural, gentle elliptical way to ask about a change of heart.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses non-past 変わりますか, which doesn't fit asking about a decision just made. C's どうでしたか asks about an evaluation, not the reason.

contrast_examples.en: Why the change of heart? (natural ellipsis)

contrast_examples.jp: なぜ気が変わったのですか。
contrast_examples.en: Why did you change your mind? (fuller)

prompt.context_jp: 藤本が涙ながらに後悔を語る
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural as a father's quiet, broken wish?

choices.text: 一度でいいから "お父さん"って 言ってもらいたかった
一度でもよくて "お父さん"を言われたい
一回だけ "お父さん"を話してくれたかった

feedback.correct_en: 一度でいいから … 言ってもらいたかった uses the idiomatic 'even just once' with the natural passive-benefactive ending for a heartfelt past wish.
feedback.incorrect_en: B's 言われたい sounds mechanical and 一度でもよくて is unnatural phrasing. C uses 話す (talk/discuss) which doesn't fit calling someone 'Dad.'

contrast_examples.jp: 一度でいいから言ってほしかった。
contrast_examples.en: I wanted him to say it, even just once.

contrast_examples.jp: "お父さん"と呼んでほしかった。
contrast_examples.en: I wanted him to call me 'Dad.'
